arxiv-2008-12358.title: The equality case in Cheeger’s and Buser’s inequalities on 𝖱𝖢𝖣 \mathsf{RCD} spaces Thanks: Nicolò De Ponti: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati (SISSA), Trieste, Italy, email: ndeponti@sissa.it Thanks: Andrea Mondino: Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford, UK, email: Andrea.Mond
arxiv-2008-12358.creator: Nicolò De Ponti, Andrea Mondino, Daniele Semola
arxiv-2008-12358.description: Abstract . We prove that the sharp Buser’s inequality obtained in the framework of 𝖱𝖢𝖣 ⁡ ( 1 , ∞ ) \mathsf{RCD}(1,\infty) spaces by the first two authors [ 29 ] is rigid, i.e. equality is obtained if and only if the space splits isomorphically a Gaussian. The result is new even in the smooth setting.

arxiv-2012-00745.title: Double machine learning for sample selection models
arxiv-2012-00745.creator: Michela Bia*, Martin Huber**, and Lukáš Lafférs+
arxiv-2012-00745.description: Abstract Abstract: This paper considers the evaluation of discretely distributed treatments when outcomes are only observed for a subpopulation due to sample selection or outcome attrition. For identification, we combine a selection-on-observables assumption for treatment assignment with either selection-on-observables or instrumental variable assumptions concerning the outcome attrition/sample selection process.

arxiv-2101-05732.title: Borel Colouring Bad Sequences
arxiv-2101-05732.creator: Keegan Dasilva Barbosa
arxiv-2101-05732.description: Abstract Every better quasi-order codifies a Borel graph that does not contain a copy of the shift graph. It is known that there is a better quasi-order that codes a Borel graph with infinite Borel chromatic number, though one has yet to be explicitly constructed. In this paper, we show that examples cannot be constructed via standard methods.

arxiv-2201-11820.title: On the number of p p -hypergeometric solutions of KZ equations
arxiv-2201-11820.creator: Alexander Varchenko
arxiv-2201-11820.description: Abstract . It is known that solutions of the KZ equations can be written in the form of multidimensional hypergeometric integrals. In 2017 in a joint paper of the author with V. Schechtman the construction of hypergeometric solutions was modified, and solutions of the KZ equations modulo a prime number p p were constructed.

arxiv-2204-11999.title: On the current failure—but bright future—of topology-driven biological network alignment
arxiv-2204-11999.creator: Siyue Wang, Xiaoyin Chen, Brent J. Frederisy, Benedict A. Mbakogu, Amy D. Kanne, Pasha Khosravi, Wayne B. Hayes
arxiv-2204-11999.description: Abstract Since the function of a protein is defined by its interaction partners, and since we expect similar interaction patterns across species, the alignment of protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks between species, based on network topology alone, should uncover functionally related proteins across species.

arxiv-2301-09965.title: Determinants of Laplacians on random hyperbolic surfaces
arxiv-2301-09965.creator: By Frédéric Naud
arxiv-2301-09965.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by By Frédéric Naud. For sequences ( X j ) (X_{j}) of random closed hyperbolic surfaces with volume Vol ⁡ ( X j ) \mathrm{Vol}(X_{j}) tending to infinity, we prove that there exists a universal constant E > 0 E>0 such that for all ϵ > 0 \epsilon>0 , the regularized determinant of the Laplacian satisfies log det ( Δ X j ) Vol ⁡ ( X j ) ∈ [ E − ϵ , E + ϵ ] \frac{\log\det(\Delta_{X_{j}})}{\mathrm{Vol}(X_{j})}\in[E-\epsilon,E+\epsilon] with high probability as j

arxiv-2309-00144.title: Multi Agent DeepRL based Joint Power and Subchannel Allocation in IAB networks
arxiv-2309-00144.creator: Lakshya Jagadish 1 , Banashree Sarma 1 , R. Manivasakan 1
arxiv-2309-00144.description: Abstract Integrated Access and Backhauling (IAB) is a viable approach for meeting the unprecedented need for higher data rates of future generations, acting as a cost-effective alternative to dense fiber-wired links. The design of such networks with constraints usually results in an optimization problem of non-convex and combinatorial nature.

arxiv-2311-00059.title: The Generative AI Paradox: “What It Can Create, It May Not Understand”
arxiv-2311-00059.creator: Peter West Ximing Lu Nouha Dziri Faeze Brahman Linjie Li, Jena D. Hwang Liwei Jiang Jillian Fisher Abhilasha Ravichander, Khyathi Raghavi Chandu Benjamin Newman, Pang Wei Koh Allyson Ettinger Yejin Choi, [0.1cm] University of Washington Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence[0.1cm] {pawest,linj
arxiv-2311-00059.description: Abstract The recent wave of generative AI has sparked unprecedented global attention, with both excitement and concern over potentially superhuman levels of artificial intelligence: models now take only seconds to produce outputs that would challenge or exceed the capabilities even of expert humans.

arxiv-2405-20192.title: TAIA : Large Language Models are Out-of-Distribution Data Learners
arxiv-2405-20192.creator: Shuyang Jiang, Yusheng Liao *, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang †
arxiv-2405-20192.description: Abstract Fine-tuning on task-specific question-answer pairs is a predominant method for enhancing the performance of instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) on downstream tasks. However, in certain specialized domains, such as healthcare or harmless content generation, it is nearly impossible to obtain a large volume of high-quality data that matches the downstream distribution.

arxiv-2408-06306.title: Dissecting Lepton Number Violating Interactions in the Left-Right Symmetric Model: 0 ​ ν ​ β ​ β 0\nu\beta\beta decay, Møller scattering, and collider searches
arxiv-2408-06306.creator: Gang Li, Michael J. Ramsey-Musolf, Sebastián Urrutia Quiroga, Juan Carlos Vasquez
arxiv-2408-06306.description: Abstract In the context of the left-right symmetric model, we study the interplay of neutrinoless double beta ( 0 ​ ν ​ β ​ β 0\nu\beta\beta ) decay, parity-violating Møller scattering, and high-energy colliders, resulting from the Yukawa interaction of the right-handed doubly-charged scalar to electrons, which could evade the severe constraints from charged lepton flavor violation.

arxiv-2411-11414.title: Temporal and Spatial Reservoir Ensembling Techniques for Liquid State Machines
arxiv-2411-11414.creator: Anmol Biswas, Sharvari Ashok Medhe, Raghav Singhal, Udayan Ganguly
arxiv-2411-11414.description: Abstract Reservoir computing (RC), which is an umbrella term for a class of computational methods such as Echo State Networks (ESN) and Liquid State Machines (LSM) can be thought of as describing a generic method to perform pattern recognition and temporal analysis with any system having non-linear dynamics.

arxiv-2412-10111.title: Stability of cosmological singularity-free solutions in quadratic gravity
arxiv-2412-10111.creator: Manuel Asorey, Fernando Ezquerro and Miguel Pardina
arxiv-2412-10111.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Manuel Asorey, Fernando Ezquerro and Miguel Pardina. We introduce a large family of homogeneous and isotropic cosmological solutions in quadratic gravity which are singularity-free at early and late times. This kind of smooth solutions only emerges beyond the unstable de Sitter branch 3 ​ α < β 3\alpha<\beta , α \alpha being the coupling of the R 2 R^{2} term and − β -\beta the coupling of the R μ ​ ν 2 R_{\mu\nu}^{2} term.

arxiv-2504-02963.title: Digital Forensics in the Age of Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-02963.creator: Zhipeng Yin, Zichong Wang, Weifeng Xu, Jun Zhuang, Pallab Mozumder, Antoinette Smith, Wenbin Zhang
arxiv-2504-02963.description: Abstract Digital forensics plays a pivotal role in modern investigative processes, utilizing specialized methods to systematically collect, analyze, and interpret digital evidence for judicial proceedings. However, traditional digital forensic techniques are primarily based on manual labor-intensive processes, which become increasingly insufficient with the rapid growth and complexity of digital data.

arxiv-2504-15109.title: New Heintze-Karcher type inequalities in sub-static warped product manifolds
arxiv-2504-15109.creator: Haizhong Li, Yong Wei, Botong Xu
arxiv-2504-15109.description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove Heintze-Karcher type inequalities involving the shifted mean curvature for smooth bounded domains in certain sub-static warped product manifolds. In particular, we prove a Heintze-Karcher-type inequality for non mean-convex domains in the hyperbolic space. As applications, we obtain uniqueness results for hypersurfaces satisfying a class of curvature equations.

arxiv-2505-11535.title: Bridging Human Oversight and Black-box Driver Assistance: Vision-Language Models for Predictive Alerting in Lane Keeping Assist Systems
arxiv-2505-11535.creator: Yuhang Wang Hao Zhou * yuhangw@usf.edu haozhou1@usf.edu
arxiv-2505-11535.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuhang Wang Hao Zhou * yuhangw@usf.edu haozhou1@usf.edu. Lane Keeping Assist (LKA) systems, while increasingly prevalent, often suffer from unpredictable real-world failures, largely due to their opaque, black-box nature, which limits driver anticipation and trust. To bridge the gap between automated assistance and effective human oversight, we present LKAlert , a novel supervisory alert system that leverages Vision-Language Model (VLM) to forecast potential LKA risk 1–3 seconds in advance.

arxiv-2508-00073.title: The Simons Observatory: Assessing the Impact of Dust Complexity on the Recovery of Primordial B B -modes
arxiv-2508-00073.creator: Yiqi Liu, Susanna Azzoni, Susan E. Clark, Brandon S. Hensley, Léo Vacher, David Alonso, Carlo Baccigalupi, Michael L. Brown, Alessandro Carones, Jens Chluba, Jo Dunkley, Carlos Hervías-Caimapo, Bradley R. Johnson, Nicoletta Krachmalnicoff, Giuseppe Puglisi, Mathieu Remazeilles, Kevin Wolz
arxiv-2508-00073.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yiqi Liu, Susanna Azzoni, Susan E. Clark, Brandon S. Hensley, Léo Vacher, David Alonso, Carlo Baccigalupi, Michael L. Brown, Alessandro Carones, Jens Chluba, Jo Dunkley, Carlos Hervías-Caimapo, Bradley R. Johnson, Nicoletta Krachmalnicoff, Giuseppe Puglisi, Mathieu Remazeilles, Kevin Wolz. We investigate how dust foreground complexity can affect measurements of the tensor-to-scalar ratio, r r , in the context of the Simons Observatory, using a cross-spectrum component separation analysis.

arxiv-2509-06467.title: Does DINOv3 Set a New Medical Vision Standard? A Comprehensive Benchmark on 2D/3D Classification and Segmentation
arxiv-2509-06467.creator: Che Liu, Yinda Chen, Haoyuan Shi, Jinpeng Lu, Bailiang Jian, Jiazhen Pan, Linghan Cai, Jiayi Wang, Yundi Zhang, Jun Li, Cosmin I. Bercea, Cheng Ouyang, Chen Chen, Zhiwei Xiong, Benedikt Wiestler, Christian Wachinger, Daniel Rueckert, Wenjia Bai, Rossella Arcucci
arxiv-2509-06467.description: Abstract The advent of large-scale vision foundation models, pre-trained on diverse natural images, has marked a paradigm shift in computer vision. However, how the frontier vision foundation models’ efficacies transfer to specialized domains remains such as medical imaging remains an open question.

arxiv-2510-21538.title: InterpDetect: Interpretable Signals for Detecting Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
arxiv-2510-21538.creator: Likun Tan, Kuan-Wei Huang, Joy Shi, Kevin Wu
arxiv-2510-21538.description: Abstract Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) integrates external knowledge to mitigate hallucinations, yet models often generate outputs inconsistent with retrieved content. Accurate hallucination detection requires disentangling the contributions of external context and parametric knowledge, which prior methods typically conflate. We investigate the mechanisms underlying RAG hallucinations and find they arise when later-layer FFN modules disproportionately inject parametric knowledge into the residual stream.

britannica-1911-east-london.title: East London (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-east-london.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-east-london.description: Article 'East London' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 8), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. East London owes its foundation to the necessities of the Kaffir war of 1846–1847. The British, requiring a port nearer the scene of war than those then existing, selected a site at the mouth of the Buffalo river, and in 1847 the first cargo of military stores was landed. A fort, named Glamorgan, was built, and the place permanently occupied.

pmc-10589959.title: Impact of stress hyperglycemia ratio on mortality in patients with critical acute myocardial infarction: insight from american MIMIC-IV and the chinese CIN-II study
pmc-10589959.creator: Jin Liu, Yang Zhou, Haozhang Huang, Rui Liu, Yu Kang, Tingting Zhu, Jielan Wu, Yuwei Gao, Yuqi Li, Chenyang Wang, Shiqun Chen, Nianjin Xie, Xueyan Zheng, Ruilin Meng, Yong Liu, Ning Tan, Fei Gao
pmc-10589959.description: BackgroundAmong patients with acute coronary syndrome and percutaneous coronary intervention, stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) is primarily associated with short-term unfavorable outcomes. However, the relationship between SHR and long-term worsen prognosis in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients admitted in intensive care unit (ICU) are not fully investigated, especially in those with different ethnicity.

pmc-11547156.title: Chest Tubes and Pleural Drainage: History and Current Status in Pleural Disease Management
pmc-11547156.creator: Claudio Sorino, David Feller-Kopman, Federico Mei, Michele Mondoni, Sergio Agati, Giampietro Marchetti, Najib M Rahman, Teruhiko Imamura, Epaminondas G Zakynthinos
pmc-11547156.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Thoracostomy and chest tube placement are key procedures in treating pleural diseases involving the accumulation of fluids (e.g., malignant effusions, serous fluid, pus, or blood) or air (pneumothorax) in the pleural cavity. Initially described by Hippocrates and refined through the centuries, chest drainage achieved a historical milestone in the 19th century with the creation of closed drainage systems to prevent the entry of air into the pleural space and reduce infection risk.

pmc-12511291.title: Thermal-intensified interfacial polymerization enables ultra-selective reverse osmosis membrane for toxic micropollutant removal
pmc-12511291.creator: Shenghua Zhou, Lu Elfa Peng, Wenyu Liu, Hao Guo, Chuyang Y Tang
pmc-12511291.description: Polyamide reverse osmosis (RO) membranes are widely used in seawater desalination and wastewater reuse, yet often fail to remove small toxic micropollutants. Herein, we develop a thermal-intensified interfacial polymerization (TIP) strategy to fabricate highly selective RO membranes against various micropollutants. Facile heating accelerates amine monomer diffusion, intensifying interfacial polymerization to form a highly crosslinked polyamide membrane.

pmc-12609934.title: Magnesium Plus Hydrogen Fertilization Enhances Mg Uptake, Growth Performance and Monoterpenoid Indole Alkaloid Biosynthesis in Catharanthus roseus
pmc-12609934.creator: Chaoqin Ou, Xinmin Qiu, Qian Zhao, Ding Ding, Yaojie Zhang, Ji De, Yuliang Wang, Kexuan Tang, Haiyan Yang, Qifang Pan
pmc-12609934.description: Magnesium and hydrogen fertilization have been reported to contribute to plant growth and metabolite production. Simultaneous fertilization of magnesium and hydrogen is a promising strategy for plant development and secondary metabolism, but remains unexplored in Catharanthus roseus (L.) G.Don, which produces varieties of monoterpenoid indole alkaloids (MIAs).

pmc-12657609.title: Pediatric non-infectious inflammatory lytic lesions of the skull: The pitfalls of diagnosis
pmc-12657609.creator: Peggy Alkefrawi, Sylvain Breton, Geneviève Baujat, Isabelle Melki, Benjamin Fournier, Brigitte Bader-Meunier
pmc-12657609.description: Chronic non-bacterial osteomyelitis of the skull is a rare entity that should be taken into account in the differential diagnosis of lacunar lesions of the skull. Here, we present four challenging cases of non-infectious inflammatory lytic lesions of the neurocranium with a diagnostic delay of one to five years.

pmc-12691966.title: Gold Nanoparticles as a Possible Tool to Untangle Some Structural Features of the Gluten Network
pmc-12691966.creator: Davide Emide, Giovanni D’Auria, Stefania Iametti, Alberto Barbiroli, Mauro Marengo, Gianfranco Mamone, Pasquale Ferranti, Francesco Bonomi
pmc-12691966.description: Aqueous semolina suspensions were reacted with spherical gold nanoparticles (AuNPs, nominal diameter, 20 nm) to assess the accessibility of cysteine thiols in durum wheat proteins, focusing on network-forming gluten proteins. Unlike small thiol reagents, covalent bond formation between gold ions on the AuNPs surface and protein thiols was greatly facilitated by the addition of 1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS).

pmc-12794104.title: Electrochemical corrosion behavior of cast and SLM Co-Cr dental alloys in artificial saliva with variable pH
pmc-12794104.creator: Alexandra Elena Biculescu, Anca Iuliana Popescu, Ioana Ana Maria Ciorniciuc, Ruxandra Nicolette Voinea-Georgescu, Raluca Monica Comăneanu, Costin Coman, Anca Monica Dobrescu
pmc-12794104.description: This study compares the corrosion resistance of two cobalt–chromium (Co–Cr) dental alloys manufactured by casting (Wirobond SG) and Selective Laser Melting (Mediloy S-Co). Standardized disc specimens were analyzed morphologically (SEM), elementally (EDS), and electrochemically (OCP and Tafel plots). Tests were performed in Carter-Brugirard artificial saliva (pH 4.9 and 6.8) at 37 ± 1°C.

pmc-13295974.title: Macroporous Resin Purification of Phenolics from Penthorum chinense Leaves: Phenolic Identification, Composition Analysis, and Biological Activities
pmc-13295974.creator: Qian Lai, Junlin Deng, Manyou Yu, Lu Gan, Yongqing Zhu, Chen Xia, Youmin Ying, Zhuoya Xiang
pmc-13295974.description: In this study, 20% ethanol elution fraction(PC-20), 40% ethanol elution fraction(PC-40), 60% ethanol elution fraction(PC-60), and 80% ethanol elution fraction (PC-80)of Penthorum chinense polyphenols were obtained using AB-8 macroporous resin . Their in vitro bioactivities were compared to explore potential applications.

pmc-13338385.title: Prospects of DNA nanotechnology in stroke repair and regeneration
pmc-13338385.creator: Krupa Kansara, Keya Jantrania, Shaivee Chokshi, Dhiraj Bhatia, Ashutosh Kumar
pmc-13338385.description: Stroke remains a significant global cause of death and long-term disability, with limited effective treatments for repairing and regenerating damaged brain tissue. Conventional therapy primarily focuses on acute care and preventing recurrence, but it falls short in restoring lost neural function.

pmc-13512592.title: Execution-Aware Segmented Modeling of Temporally Correlated Flux-Induced Phase Noise in Quantum Circuits
pmc-13512592.creator: Hongxiang Zhu, Xinxuan Chen, Hui-Hai Zhao, Feng Wu, Zhaofeng Su

pmc-13581567.title: Isolation and Characterization of bovine parainfluenza virus type 3 genotype C from brown cattle with respiratory disease in Yili, Xinjiang, China
pmc-13581567.creator: Xiuyu Zhang, Xingxing Liu, Guiling Wu, Qiang Fu, Lei zhang, Xintong Chen, Chuanfeng Wang, Jinxin Xie, Panpan Tong
pmc-13581567.description: PurposeIn winter 2025, a severe respiratory disease outbreak occurred in brown cattle in Yili, Xinjiang, China.ResultsWe detected bovine parainfluenza virus type 3 (BPIV-3) in all clinical samples from affected animals and successfully isolated the virus. Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis classified the isolates as genotype C, which is currently the predominant lineage circulating in Chinese cattle herds.
